answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a costly resource before it can transact, like a crystal lattice that only forms under pressure. A newcomer must lock collateral or complete attested work, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs money and time. Honest agents build reputation over seasons, like bees returning to the same meadow each year, while a sybil swarm has no history to harvest. The nectar, access to markets and rewards, flows only to identities whose stake and record prove they are one real participant, making mass fakery unprofitable.
